high.title: VN-Index Lost Over 113 Points in 1 Week, Expert Points to Stocks in "Oversold Zone"
high.summary: Vietnam's stock market ended the first trading week of March with negative performance as VN-Index plummeted to its lowest level in about three weeks. The index closed at 1,767 points on March 6, losing over 40 points from the previous session and evaporating over 113 points compared to the previous week - a sharp decline similar to the "tariff shock" in April 2025. Selling pressure intensified amid escalating Middle East geopolitical tensions, causing extreme investor anxiety. Apart from some sectors benefiting from oil price movements like oil & gas, chemicals, and marine transport showing positive gains, most other stock groups were deep in red. The decline reflects concerns over the geopolitical situation affecting regional markets, with experts suggesting some sectors may now be in oversold territory, potentially creating opportunities for selective investors.

high.title: USD and Oil Prices Rise Sharply Due to Middle East Conflict: How Will Exchange Rate and Inflation in Vietnam Be Affected?
high.summary: On February 28, 2026, the US coordinated with Israel to conduct airstrikes against Iran, which Iran retaliated against US and Israeli targets. This escalated Middle East tensions rapidly, increasing global geopolitical risks. Oil prices surged immediately on supply disruption fears, while cross-continental logistics supply chains face potential disruption due to skyrocketing insurance and shipping costs. The USD Index (DXY) jumped 0.8% to 98.42 points, with gold also rising, reflecting clear "risk-off" sentiment in global financial markets. For Vietnam, this creates pressure on VND/USD exchange rates and potential inflationary pressures through higher import costs. VCBS analysis suggests global capital flows are rebalancing toward safe-haven assets, which could impact emerging market currencies like the VND and complicate monetary policy decisions.

high.title: Military Bank Just Raised Deposit Interest Rates Significantly
high.summary: MB Bank has significantly increased deposit interest rates, particularly for terms of 12 months and longer. For deposits under 1 billion VND, rates for 12-18 month terms increased from 5.5% to 6.1% per annum (up 0.6 percentage points), while 24-60 month terms rose from 6.3% to 6.6% per annum (up 0.3 percentage points). Short-term rates remained unchanged. For deposits of 1 billion VND and above, similar upward adjustments were implemented. This move signals potential broader interest rate pressures in the banking system, reflecting either liquidity needs or competitive positioning. The rate increases could influence deposit flows between banks and impact overall monetary conditions in the economy.

high.title: Middle East Tensions: How Do They Affect USD Prices?
high.summary: In Vietnam, USD exchange rates have shown recent upward pressure. The State Bank of Vietnam's central rate is currently at 25,057 VND/USD, rising consecutively by 13 dong over the past week. Commercial banks quote USD around 26,029-26,309 VND/USD (bid-ask), while the free market trades at higher levels around 26,850-26,880 VND/USD. Deputy Governor Pham Thanh Ha noted that Middle East tensions have driven global oil prices up 8-13% in just a few days, creating additional inflationary pressure globally. This has made major central banks more cautious about interest rate cuts, with some signaling potential rate increases. The developments suggest continued USD strength and VND pressure, with implications for Vietnam's import costs and monetary policy flexibility.

medium.title: BIDV Bank Interest Rates March 2025: Which Term Has the Highest Interest Rate?
medium.summary: BIDV maintains stable deposit rates with highest rates of 5.3% per annum for 24-36 month terms. Short-term rates range from 2.1-3.5% per annum depending on maturity, while 12-18 month terms offer 5.2% per annum. The rate structure reflects current banking sector liquidity conditions and competitive positioning.

medium.title: Vietcombank Latest Interest Rates March 2026
medium.summary: Vietcombank maintains stable deposit rate structure with highest rates at 5.3% per annum for 24+ month terms, applied to both counter and online deposits. The bank continues its conservative rate policy amid current market conditions, with rates ranging from 0.1% for demand deposits to the maximum 5.3% for long-term deposits.

medium.title: Good News for All People Borrowing from Banks, Finance Companies
medium.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam is seeking feedback on draft regulations that would raise the small loan threshold from 100 million to 400 million VND for credit institutions. Small loans would not require feasible capital usage plans, significantly easing borrowing procedures for retail customers and improving access to credit for individuals and small businesses.

medium.title: Real Estate Companies Push Bond Channel as Credit Tightens
medium.summary: With over 44,000 real estate companies nationwide but limited public listings, the sector is turning to bond markets for medium and long-term funding as bank credit remains tightly controlled. Real estate bond yields have shown upward trends since 2025, though liquidity remains low and investor confidence hasn't fully recovered from the 2021 bond crisis.

medium.title: Expert: Stock Market Next Week Could Fall to 1,700 Points
medium.summary: Following a volatile first week of March with VN-Index dropping 112.49 points (-5.98%) to 1,767.84 points, experts warn of potential further decline to 1,700 points. Despite high liquidity (50% above 20-week average), foreign investors continued strong net selling worth over 6,000 billion VND, just one month before FTSE Russell's potential market upgrade consideration.

medium.title: Hot: Proposal to Reduce Import Tax on Gasoline and Oil to 0%
medium.summary: Ministry of Finance proposes reducing preferential import tax rates on petroleum products and raw materials to 0% due to Middle East conflicts affecting global oil supply. Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has disrupted 20 million barrels daily, forcing Asian refineries to cut capacity and raising Singapore market prices significantly.
